title: "Callout Markdown Bug"
format:

# Reproducible Callout Captions

::: callout-note
## Text in **strong**, and some `code`

This is a note callout whose caption should render **bold** text and inline `code`, but instead will appear unformatted or cause an error.
:::

::: callout-note
## Using the multi-assignment `%<-%` operator

The `%<-%` operator is described here.
:::

::: callout-note
## Text, separated with comma

This caption contains a comma which will be mis-parsed as a tcolorbox option key.
:::
1.explanation: Save the above content as, for example, `bug-callout.qmd`. Then run `quarto render bug-callout.qmd --to pdf`. The PDF build will (a) drop Markdown styling in the first caption, and (b) emit LaTeX errors for the `%<-%` and comma captions, demonstrating the bug in callout caption processing.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering a PDF with callouts whose header (caption) contains Markdown formatting or special characters (e.g. **strong**, `code`, %, comma), the Lua filter currently uses pandoc.utils.stringify(), emitting the raw text (including **, backticks, commas) directly into the tcolorbox “title” option. This leads to (1) lack of Markdown formatting in the caption, and (2) LaTeX errors when special characters (%, commas) are interpreted as tcolorbox keys or unescaped tokens.
